taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes Dubois et al. (2021) place it in genus Aquarana; NatureServe keeps Lithobates and calls the generic arrangement of American ranids controversial.
fieldMarks: Adults about 8.2-16.5 cm snout-vent; green, olive or brown with dark spots toward the hind end; white-grey belly; smooth skin.
Resembles American bullfrog but the snout is much more pointed; hind feet almost fully webbed.
Call: 1-13 short, loud pig-like grunts; choruses sound like a roar.
behavior: Fully aquatic and confined to wetlands; males call floating in water and are territorial.
Feeds nocturnally, mostly on arthropods, especially crayfish (20-75% of diet).
Chorusing is typically nocturnal per NatureServe, while Animal Diversity Web says it typically calls by day.
Burrows into mud when wetlands dry or to hibernate (Nov-March) in colder regions.
habitat: Permanent lakes, ponds, swamps, marshes and streams, especially with abundant emergent or floating vegetation; old rice fields.
range: Southern South Carolina to southern Florida and west to southeastern Texas; introduced in the Bahamas and northern Puerto Rico.

lookalikes.howToTell: Pig frog has a much more pointed snout and is smaller than the bullfrog.
